high.title: [Bond Market - Weekly] U.S.-Iran Conflict May Surprise Markets, But Here's What to Watch
high.summary:
South Korea's bond market is bracing for a soft open this week (June 29–July 3) as geopolitical risk from the U.S.-Iran conflict injects fresh uncertainty into global fixed income markets. U.S. President Trump announced via Truth Social on June 27 that U.S. aircraft had struck Iranian military targets, reigniting risk-off sentiment that could pressure Korean government bond (KTB) yields to move in a flight-to-safety pattern. However, analysts note that given the repeated cycles of escalation and de-escalation in U.S.-Iran negotiations, markets may ultimately treat this as part of a longer negotiation process rather than a structural geopolitical rupture — potentially limiting the magnitude of any bond market dislocation. For KRW traders, a sustained risk-off episode could weaken the Won against the USD as capital flows toward safe-haven assets. Bond investors should monitor whether KTB yields decline (price rally) on safe-haven demand or rise if global risk assets stabilize quickly. The trajectory of U.S. Treasury yields this week will be the critical external anchor for KTB pricing.

---

high.title: [FX-Weekly] Dollar-Won Tests 1,550 Level Amid US-Iran Military Clash - Authorities' Intervention in Focus
high.summary: The USD/KRW exchange rate is expected to consolidate around the 1,540 won level this week, with potential tests of the 1,550 level given heightened geopolitical risk following the US-Iran military confrontation. Last week, the pair gradually drifted higher within a 1,530–1,540 range as foreign investors maintained a persistent selling stance in Korean equities, adding structural downward pressure on the won through equity-related capital outflows. The dual headwinds of geopolitical uncertainty — which typically triggers risk-off flows and USD demand — and continued foreign equity selling create a challenging near-term backdrop for KRW bulls. Market participants will closely watch whether Korean authorities deploy smoothing operations or verbal intervention if the rate approaches or breaches the 1,550 psychological threshold. **Key risk factors to monitor:** (1) trajectory of oil prices given Hormuz Strait tensions (higher oil = wider Korean current account deficit = KRW negative), (2) pace and magnitude of foreign equity outflows, and (3) any BOK or MoF intervention signals. For bond traders, a weaker KRW at these levels may complicate BOK's rate-cutting calculus in the near term.

high.title: Dollar-Won Rate to Fall in Q3... Opportunity for Won-Denominated Bonds in Three Months
high.summary: DB Securities researcher Moon Hong-chul projects near-term upward pressure on USD/KRW, driven by passive fund rebalancing as foreign investors' share of the domestic equity market has grown excessively — triggering mechanical selling of Korean stocks and KRW as these funds rebalance back to benchmark weights. However, the medium-term view is more constructive: with oil prices stabilizing and domestic interest rates stabilizing, Moon argues that won-denominated bonds (KTBs) should present a genuine buying opportunity within approximately three months, coinciding with an expected Q3 pullback in the dollar-won rate. **Implications:** This is a meaningful signal for international fixed-income investors — the near-term entry point for KTBs may not yet be optimal given residual FX headwinds, but a Q3 tactical allocation window is being flagged. Traders should watch for confirmation signals: USD/KRW reversal from the 1,540–1,550 zone, stabilization of foreign equity flows, and any BOK forward guidance that supports the rate-cut narrative underpinning bond demand.

medium.title: Consumer Lending Hits 13.1 Trillion Won as Bank Regulations Drive Credit and Secured Loan Growth
medium.summary:
Outstanding loans from consumer finance companies surged in the second half of last year, reaching 13.1 trillion Won, as major lenders expanded personal credit and secured lending. The growth is directly linked to tightening household lending regulations at commercial banks, which appear to be displacing borrowing demand toward secondary and non-bank financial institutions — a dynamic regulators typically view with concern. This regulatory arbitrage trend is relevant for bond and FX investors as it signals continued stress in Korean household balance sheets and complicates the Bank of Korea's monetary easing calculus. If credit risk migrates to less regulated corners of the financial system, the BOK may face pressure to maintain a cautious stance on rate cuts even as growth slows. Watch for any FSS follow-up regulatory action targeting consumer finance companies.

---

medium.title: US-Iran Escalation: Airstrikes and Strait of Hormuz Tensions Risk-Off Signal for KRW
medium.summary:
🔗 https://en.infomaxai.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=127475
🔗 https://en.infomaxai.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=127471

These three articles collectively report on an escalating US-Iran military confrontation, with the US Central Command conducting multiple rounds of airstrikes on Iranian missile storage facilities, drone bases, and coastal radar installations following continued Iranian attacks on commercial vessels — most recently the container ship *Ever Lovely* — passing through the Strait of Hormuz. President Trump issued an explicit existential warning to Iran via Truth Social, signaling potential for further escalation.

**Relevance to KRW and Korean markets:** While none of these articles directly address Korean financial markets, the geopolitical escalation carries meaningful indirect implications for KRW traders and bond investors. Key transmission channels include:

1. **Oil price shock risk:** The Strait of Hormuz is a critical artery for global energy flows. Any prolonged disruption would sharply lift Brent crude prices, widening Korea's import bill and deteriorating the current account — a structurally bearish force for KRW.
2. **Risk-off USD demand:** Geopolitical flare-ups of this magnitude typically trigger safe-haven flows into USD and JPY, putting pressure on EM currencies including KRW.
3. **Korean equity outflows:** Heightened global risk aversion could accelerate foreign selling of KOSPI equities, adding to KRW depreciation pressure.
4. **BOK watch:** If oil-driven inflation re-accelerates alongside a weaker KRW, the BOK may face a more complicated rate path.

**What to watch:** Monitor Brent crude futures closely; a sustained move above key resistance levels would materially shift the KRW/USD outlook toward weakness. Watch for any BOK verbal intervention if KRW approaches the 1,400+ range.

medium.title: ECB's Schnabel Signals Further Rate Hikes to Combat Inflation
medium.summary:
ECB Executive Board member Isabel Schnabel, speaking at the Petersberg Summer Dialogue in Germany, reiterated the ECB's commitment to additional rate hikes to bring inflation back to its 2% medium-term target. She flagged that energy price shocks risk feeding into broader inflationary pressures, suggesting the ECB's tightening cycle has further to run.

**Relevance to KRW and Korean markets:** A persistently hawkish ECB reinforces global rate divergence dynamics. With the BOK navigating its own inflation-versus-growth trade-off, continued ECB tightening keeps global risk-free rates elevated, sustaining pressure on EM bond spreads including Korean government bonds (KTBs). A stronger EUR resulting from hawkish ECB signals may offer some modest USD softening relief for KRW, but the broader environment of high developed-market rates remains a headwind for foreign inflows into Korean fixed income. Fund managers should monitor whether ECB hawkishness further compresses the relative attractiveness of KTBs versus European sovereigns.

medium.title: KOSPI Breaks 9,000 Points for First Time in History; Kosdaq Lags Behind in Chip-Led Rally
medium.summary: South Korea's benchmark KOSPI index closed above the 9,000-point threshold for the first time in its history on Thursday, propelled by mounting expectations of a prolonged global memory chip shortage and sustained bullish sentiment around Korea's semiconductor sector. Despite this landmark equity milestone, the Kosdaq — celebrating its 30th anniversary — has notably failed to participate in the rally, remaining in KOSPI's shadow. Additionally, the government is reportedly moving to prohibit listed companies from bringing spun-off units to market, and a two-tier listing league system is being introduced. For KRW and bond traders, the KOSPI's historic level signals strong foreign equity inflows which could provide mild KRW support, though the divergence between KOSPI and Kosdaq warrants monitoring as a risk sentiment indicator. Watch for whether sustained foreign buying in equities translates into broader capital flow dynamics affecting USD/KRW.

medium.title: Deputy PM Koo Yun-chul Pledges Full Government Support for Corporate Regional Investment
medium.summary: Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Koo Yun-chul signaled continued government commitment to directing corporate investment toward regional areas, framing it as a critical front in global advanced industry competition. While primarily an industrial policy statement, it reflects the fiscal stance of Korea's economic leadership — relevant context for assessing government spending trajectories and any potential bond supply implications. The emphasis on "ultra-gap" competitiveness suggests the administration remains focused on structural industrial policy rather than near-term fiscal stimulus, which carries limited immediate impact on KRW or yields but is worth monitoring for broader fiscal outlook signals.

medium.title: [New York Foreign Exchange Market - Weekly] Japan Intervention Fears Persist as US Jobs Data Complicates Market Calculus
medium.summary: The dollar is expected to open the week on a firm footing globally, supported by safe-haven demand following the weekend US-Iran military confrontation. Dollar-yen is approaching the critical 162 level, raising the probability of Japanese FX intervention — a development with spillover implications for KRW given the historical co-movement between JPY and KRW in risk-off environments. Weaker-than-expected US jobs data (if realized) could paradoxically create the ideal intervention window for Japanese authorities by triggering a sharp yen snap-back. For KRW traders, a stronger dollar globally combined with JPY weakness creates a complex backdrop: KRW may face independent selling pressure while any BOJ/MoF intervention could temporarily shift regional FX dynamics. The ECB Sintra forum — where Fed Chair Powell may also appear — could provide additional signals on global rate coordination that affect USD sentiment broadly.

medium.title: Iran Warns Against Attempts to Bypass Hormuz Strait Route - 'Will Escalate Tensions'
medium.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi reaffirmed Iran's control over Hormuz Strait maritime traffic management, stating that full reopening of the waterway following recent obstacles remains Tehran's responsibility under a framework agreement with the US. While a deal appears to be in progress, Iran's warning against bypass attempts signals continued geopolitical friction. **KRW relevance:** Korea is heavily dependent on Middle East oil imports transiting the Strait of Hormuz. Sustained disruption or price spikes in crude would widen Korea's trade deficit, increase inflationary pressure, and structurally weaken KRW — compounding the existing pressures noted in this week's FX outlook. Any re-escalation should be treated as a KRW-negative tail risk event.
